conflicts.conflict: SRE requires a 24h soak before expanding beyond canary, while ConsumerSubsystem requires keeping legacy routing config support until all 19 locations are confirmed healthy; this favors delaying any schema- or behavior-dependent cleanup until the end.
SRE requires an approved maintenance window excluding Friday afternoon, while ProductPM requires rollout outside launch windows and major customer events; these timing windows may not overlap.

BackendOwner wants to proceed from staged rollout only after traffic asymmetry normalizes, while Security requires explicit compliance sign-off for global reachability impact; both block expansion and must be satisfied before broader rollout.

Security requires customer/partner notification before visible routing changes, while ProductPM also requires customer notice before any customer-visible routing change; both are blocking and need sequencing before rollout.

DataPlatform pauses expansion if propagation lag slips below threshold and SRE pauses on upstream instability/customer impact; these are parallel blocking gates that can halt the same batch for different reasons.

BackendOwner wants small batches that only expand when healthy, while DataPlatform requires a small initial batch and no expansion until propagation lag is acceptable; the rollout granularity must satisfy both or remain paused.

ProductPM requires support briefing and named escalation before customer-visible changes, while ConsumerSubsystem requires legacy routing config support during the staged rollout; both constrain the rollout process and support path.
